questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Complex Conjugate of a Complex Matrix
questions.problem: Find $B=\overset{―}{A}$, where $A=[\begin{aligned}7-\text{i} & 6+4\text{i} \\ 7-4\text{i} & 4+9\text{i}\end{aligned}].$ What is the value of ${b}_{12}-{b}_{21}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}7-\text{i} & 6+4\text{i} \\ 7-4\text{i} & 4+9\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{7-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{6+4\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{7-4\text{i}} & \overset{―}{4+9\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7+\text{i} & 6-4\text{i} \\ 7+4\text{i} & 4-9\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${b}_{12}-{b}_{21}=(6-4\text{i})-(7+4\text{i})=-1-8\text{i}.$

questions.problem:
Find $B=\overset{―}{A}$, where
$A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3-2\text{i} & 4\text{i} \\ -1-3\text{i} & 5 & 3-5\text{i} \\ 2+\text{i} & -5-\text{i} & -3+3\text{i}\end{aligned}].$ What is the value of ${b}_{31}+{b}_{32}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3-2\text{i} & 4\text{i} \\ -1-3\text{i} & 5 & 3-5\text{i} \\ 2+\text{i} & -5-\text{i} & -3+3\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{-4} & \overset{―}{3-2\text{i}} & \overset{―}{4\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{-1-3\text{i}} & \overset{―}{5} & \overset{―}{3-5\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{2+\text{i}} & \overset{―}{-5-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{-3+3\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3+2\text{i} & -4\text{i} \\ -1+3\text{i} & 5 & 3+5\text{i} \\ 2-\text{i} & -5+\text{i} & -3-3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${b}_{31}+{b}_{32}=(2-\text{i})+(-5+\text{i})=-3.$

questions.problem: Find the imaginary part of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1-7\text{i} & 2-4\text{i} \\ 6\text{i} & -5\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1-7\text{i} & 2-4\text{i} \\ 6\text{i} & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-7\text{i} & 2-4\text{i} \\ 0+6\text{i} & -5+0\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-7 & -4 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{Im}(A)=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -4 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem: If $\,\text{Re}(x)=[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,\text{Im}(x)=[\begin{aligned}e & f \\ g & h\end{aligned}]\,$ are the real and imaginary parts of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-3\text{i} & 5\text{i} \\ -4 & 5\end{aligned}]\,$ then what is the value of $ah-cf?$
questions.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-3\text{i} & 5\text{i} \\ -4 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0-3\text{i} & 0+5\text{i} \\ -4+0\text{i} & 5+0\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -4 & 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $a=0,c=-4,f=5$ and $h=0.$ Therefore,

$$
ah-cf=0\cdot 0-(-4)\cdot 5=20.
$$

questions.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & -2-4\text{i} \\ 3-2\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following  elementary row operations:

$$
{R}_{1}=\frac{1}{1+2\text{i}}{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}={R}_{2}+(2\text{i}-3){R}_{1}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & -2-4\text{i} \\ 3-2\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{1+2\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 3-2\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(2\text{i}-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 6-3\text{i}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 6-3\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}4\text{i} & 3-\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ 2-2\text{i} & 2-\text{i} & 1+2\text{i} \\ \text{i} & 3\text{i} & 2\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{4\text{i}} & \overset{―}{3-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{1+\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{2-2\text{i}} & \overset{―}{2-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{1+2\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{\text{i}} & \overset{―}{3\text{i}} & \overset{―}{2\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4\text{i} & 3+\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ 2+2\text{i} & 2+\text{i} & 1-2\text{i} \\ -\text{i} & -3\text{i} & -2\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $b_{11} + b_{23} = (-4\textrm{i}) + (1-2\textrm{i}) = 1-6\textrm{i}.$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Computing Components of the Real and Imaginary Parts of a Complex Matrix
canonical_examples.problem: If ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072897/assets/9e1718bbf8790a9cc89d7cc1c6dd7879f8e222f348e5a9a56fec83a1b033250d.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072897/assets/e99949f7e98aee85a040f698b15822927d7aabea1e688337d209c8e1d08850d6.png) are the real and imaginary parts of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072897/assets/642f01152b6a1717300120241f788a24098413648cd70e8d0399629f11be2254.png) then what is the value of $ad+eh?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2-3\text{i} & -5-7\text{i} \\ 1-6\text{i} & 5-9\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 & -7 \\ -6 & -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $a=2,d=5,e=-3$ and $h=-9.$ Therefore,

$$
ad+eh=2 \cdot 5 + (-3) \cdot (-9) = 37.
$$

Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 1 & 2\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ \text{i} & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(-\text{i})\cdot (1+2\text{i})+\text{i}\cdot \text{i} & (-\text{i})\cdot (1-\text{i})+\text{i}\cdot 2 \\ 1\cdot (1+2\text{i})+2\text{i}\cdot \text{i} & 1\cdot (1-\text{i})+2\text{i}\cdot 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2-\text{i})+(-1) & (-1-\text{i})+2\text{i} \\ (1+2\text{i})+(-2) & (1-\text{i})+4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & -1+\text{i} \\ -1+2\text{i} & 1+3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations to a Complex Matrix
canonical_examples.problem:
Given the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072897/assets/14a711915f94a68eb7db2995698e8f15d8a7554702d9441c826f983bdb81df23.png) find the result of applying to $A$ the following elementary row operations:

$$
R_1 := \dfrac{1}{\textrm{i}}R_1, \qquad R_2 := R_2 - 2\textrm{i}R_1
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}\text{i} & -\text{i} \\ 2+2\text{i} & 1\end{aligned}]\, &  & {R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2+2\text{i} & 1\end{aligned}]\, &  & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2\text{i}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1+2\text{i}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result is
